source.title: Exploratory Causal Inference in SAEnce
source.authors: Tommaso Mencattini; Riccardo Cadei; Francesco Locatello

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how SAE codes align with known concepts, bearing on whether SAE features function as canonical representation units. It does not test the original toy-model superposition setup or its geometry.
record.gate_note: The study discusses superposition and SAE interpretability concerns through cited work, but those citations are not its own results. Its relevant results are its own measurements of SAE-code alignment with known concepts; it does not test LLM superposition or feature geometry.
record.test_reason: The paper builds Neural Effect Search, a causal-inference method, on SAEs trained on SigLIP and DINOv2 vision features. Its code-to-concept F1 checks (Appendix E.1) are stated validations of the method's own assumptions A.1–A.2, not a test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units (V5). The seed-replication ablation (Figs 25–26) reports only NES precision and recall, not feature stability across runs. No LLM superposition, toy-model geometry, capacity or dimensionality result is reported. The alignment findings concern single-code monosemanticity against human labels, a related but different construct, so they go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it omits the main conclusion. Vanilla multiple testing over entangled SAE codes flags many leaked neurons as the test gains power, and Neural Effect Search avoids this. On the ant trial, NES recovers grooming plus a background-marking artifact. The authors note SAE neurons may not map one-to-one onto concepts and treat SAE identifiability as their strongest, unresolved assumption.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops Neural Effect Search for exploratory causal inference using foundation-model representations and SAEs. It does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method or measure its geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature alignment varies with the foundation model and SAE nonlinearity: the paper reports weaker or absent principal alignment for some concepts with DINOv2 or JumpReLU compared with SigLIP plus top-k.

fits_no_version.finding: In SAEs on SigLIP and DINOv2 features of CelebA, the best single code for a labelled attribute reaches F1 0.27–0.84. Alignment is weaker with DINOv2 and with JumpReLU, and under JumpReLU Wearing Hat has no principal code.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether human-labelled concepts in vision-model SAEs map onto a single principal code, and how this depends on the encoder and the SAE nonlinearity.

fits_no_version.finding: On the ISTAnt videos, the codes NES selected best predict grooming (F1 0.398) and a background marking artifact (F1 0.568).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether SAE codes selected by causal effect search align with domain-expert concepts.

record.problems: The SAE alignment evidence uses selected, known attributes and simple thresholded code activations; it does not establish feature stability across runs or canonical uniqueness. The paper itself identifies SAE identifiability as unresolved. Relevant code-level F1 results do not report uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant result rows omitted. Method-performance metrics for Neural Effect Search and its baselines were not included because they do not measure the SAE-feature properties named by the tested version.

untested.parts: All: no toy networks, sparsity transition or geometry.
All: no capacity or feature-importance analysis.
All: vision encoders only, and SAE recovery is not assessed as evidence of superposition.
Completeness, stability across seeds (seed replicas report only NES metrics) and canonical uniqueness of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: I moved the relation from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. The alignment numbers are explicitly framed as validating NES assumptions A.1–A.2, and no result measures V5's completeness, stability or canonicity. The reader's V5 labels are dropped. The paper's SAE k setting for the semi-synthetic SAE is internally inconsistent (Table 1: k=5; Appendix E.1 text: k=20).

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, overlap geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions.
Whether capacity pressure explains neuron polysemanticity or allocates dedicated dimensions to important features.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
Feature distribution or SAE recovery in LLMs; the study uses image encoders and ant-video data, not LLMs.
The experiments assess alignment of SAE codes with selected known concepts, but do not establish feature completeness, stability across training runs, or canonical uniqueness.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: SigLIP with SAE top-k nonlinearity
rows.operation_detail: Measured the F1-score of the most predictive SAE code for each known attribute, using code activation Zj > 0 as a binary predictor.
rows.measure: Best-code F1-score against the attribute labels
rows.locator: Appendix E.1, SigLIP with SAE top-k nonlinearity
rows.note: The authors describe a strongly aligned principal neuron and a broadly entangled long tail; the score is below perfect alignment.
rows.check: Best-code F1 (0.841, Wearing Hat, SigLIP top-k) is an assumption check for NES. It measures single-code alignment with a human label, not completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE units. The SAE row label says k=20, but Table 1 lists k=5 for the semi-synthetic SAE, so the setting is inconsistent in the paper.

rows.subject: SigLIP with SAE top-k nonlinearity
rows.operation_detail: Measured the F1-score of the most predictive SAE code for each known attribute, using code activation Zj > 0 as a binary predictor.

rows.note: The authors describe a strongly aligned principal neuron and a broadly entangled long tail; the score is below perfect alignment.
rows.check: Same as r1 (Eyeglasses, F1 0.748). This is an assumption-validation value, not a V5 measure; k is inconsistent between text (k=20) and Table 1 (k=5).

rows.subject: DINOv2 with SAE top-k nonlinearity
rows.operation_detail: Measured the F1-score of the most predictive SAE code for each known attribute, using code activation Zj > 0 as a binary predictor.
rows.measure: Best-code F1-score against the attribute labels
rows.locator: Appendix E.1, DINOv2 with SAE top-k non-linearity
rows.note: The authors say principal alignment is less evident for this concept and that it may be captured by the top three codes.
rows.check: DINOv2 top-k, Wearing Hat, F1 0.431; the authors say the concept may be spread over the top three codes. This is concept-to-code alignment, not a V5 property.

rows.subject: SigLIP with SAE JumpReLU nonlinearity
rows.operation_detail: Measured the F1-score of the most predictive SAE code for each known attribute, using code activation Zj > 0 as a binary predictor.
rows.measure: Best-code F1-score against the attribute labels
rows.locator: Appendix E.1, SigLIP with SAE JumpReLU non-linearity
rows.note: The authors state there is no clear principal component for Wearing Hat in this representation; the code captures a broader visual pattern rather than the specific concept.
rows.check: SigLIP JumpReLU, Wearing Hat, F1 0.273, with no principal code. This shows concept spread across codes under one SAE nonlinearity; it does not test canonicity or stability. 'Absent' was judged against a version the row does not measure.

rows.operation_detail: Measured the F1-score of the most predictive SAE code for each known attribute, using code activation Zj > 0 as a binary predictor.
rows.measure: Best-code F1-score against the attribute labels
rows.locator: Appendix E.1, SigLIP with SAE JumpReLU non-linearity
rows.note: The authors report a principal code for Eyeglasses, but also describe strong broad entanglement.
rows.check: SigLIP JumpReLU, Eyeglasses, F1 0.425. Assumption check, not a V5 measure.

rows.subject: ISTA NT DINOv2 with SAE
rows.operation_detail: Measured the F1-score of the most predictive SAE code for a biologist-interpreted grooming concept.
rows.measure: Best-code F1-score for predicting the concept
rows.note: The authors say the imperfect score leaves open other entangled effects or a broader representation, and that further labeling is needed to link the treatment effect on the code to the interpreted outcome.
rows.check: F1 0.398 for code 394 (grooming) on ISTAnt. It interprets a neuron that NES selected; it is part of the method's output evaluation, not a measure of SAE units as canonical.

rows.subject: ISTA NT DINOv2 with SAE
rows.operation_detail: Measured the F1-score of the most predictive SAE code for a background-position marking.
rows.measure: Best-code F1-score for predicting the characteristic
rows.note: The code identifies a finite-sample background association, not a biological effect; the result shows a code can represent an experimental artifact.
rows.check: F1 0.568 for code 550 (background marking). It interprets an NES output and does not bear on any version.
